Redwood meters embeddings by the tokens in the input. A documented Engineering finding for `rw-embed-3-large` is that its model-native tokenizer can count differently from an open-source tokenizer, including differences around Unicode normalization and whitespace; leading or trailing whitespace in the input can count too. That guidance says multiple inputs are counted individually after normalization—**batching itself doesn’t add tokens**. Your model may behave differently, so I wouldn’t assume that finding explains your exact gap.

To compare, try Redwood’s `/v1/tokenize` endpoint in staging on the exact input strings you send, preserving whitespace and Unicode, and check that your local count includes the same inputs and any retried requests. If the counts still differ, send the model name and affected request IDs; the current routing rule sends unresolved request-ID mismatches to Billing Engineering.
does batching change the token count?

No—**batching by itself doesn’t increase the total token count**. Redwood counts each embedding input individually after normalization, so the total should be the same whether those inputs are sent together or separately. The count can still differ from your local tokenizer because of tokenizer or normalization differences, or whitespace in the inputs.
